games.title: Stillwater
games.blurb: Breathe, hold, and release a ripple at just the right moment to calm the restless spirits of a moonlit pond.
games.description: A mobile-first ripple game in ink and ember. Every worry is a spirit sending waves across a dark pond. Hold to gather a breath, then let go when its ring hugs the spirit, and your gold ripple meets its wave and cancels it into stillness. Thorns are things that aren't yours to fix, and touching them only doubles them. Eight ponds teach one idea each, from the Stoic dichotomy of control to the Buddha's second arrow, and every cleared pond gives you an if-then plan to keep.
games.how: Press and hold anywhere near a spirit to breathe in, and the gold arc fills. Watch its timing ring shrink. Release when the ring turns gold and hugs the glyph. A good release calms one knot. Releasing too early does nothing, and releasing late makes a splash. Never press on a silver thorn, which doubles it. If the enso's dots run out, the pond overflows. Calm every spirit to still the water.

games.title: The Last Lantern
games.blurb: Oil runs low in the catacombs. The watchers wait past the edge of the light.
games.description: A mobile-first atmospheric exploration game. Descend three procedurally generated depths with a lantern that keeps burning low. Collect lore, solve light puzzles, and keep the flame from going out — because when it dies, the watchers close in.
games.how: Walk with a floating stick (lower half of the screen). Aim your gaze with a drag in the upper half. Hold Raise to widen the light (burns oil faster) or Lower to shrink it to an ember. Use interacts with braziers, mirrors, and seals. Find the stair at each depth after solving its light puzzle.

games.title: Bayshift
games.blurb: Drag chunky freight crates out through bay doors of their color, before the ferry whistle blows.
games.description: A mobile-first, timed block-escape puzzle on a midnight dock. Crates come in multi-cell shapes and move freely under your finger. Each one ships only through a bay door of its own color, and only if it fits through the door. Plan a route through a packed deck, park crates out of the way, and beat the clock. Eighteen handcrafted bays ramp from a single straight shot to full night-rush jams with frosted crates, rail-locked crates, shrink-wrapped crates that need two doors, and roller shutters that open only after enough loads of their color have shipped.
games.how: Drag a crate with your finger. It rides the grid on magnetic rails, following your finger along a row or column and turning a corner when you clearly move sideways. Flick it to send it gliding until it hits something, or straight out through a matching door. Push a crate into a bay door of the same color to ship it, but every row or column it covers has to fit inside the door. The clock starts on your first drag, and shipping everything with time to spare earns 3 stars. Frosted crates thaw after the number of loads shown. Railed crates only move along their track. Wrapped crates peel off one layer per door and show the color underneath. A shuttered door opens after its counter of matching loads is met. Undo is unlimited and steps back one drag or flick at a time. Break freezes the clock for 10 seconds and Lift removes one crate; each can be used once per bay. If time runs out, you can take one 30-second overtime.

games.title: Moonroost
games.blurb: One owl to every moonlit grove. They won't share a row or a column, and they won't touch, not even at a corner.
games.description: A mobile-first logic puzzle set in a hushed night wood. Each board is split into colored groves, and every grove needs exactly one owl. No two owls may share a row or a column, and none may perch beside another, even diagonally. Every board has a single solution you can reach by pure deduction, so cross out the branches that can't hold an owl, squeeze the wood down, and land each owl only where it must go. There are 36 handcrafted campaign groves that ramp from 5×5 warm-ups to 10×10 knots, plus an endless Deep wood and a fresh roost every night with a streak.
games.how: Tap a cell to cross it out, and tap again to clear it. Drag across cells to cross out a whole run; the stroke snaps to its row or column. Double-tap to land an owl. Correct owls lock in, but a wrong perch costs one of your three moons. Placed owls automatically dim every cell they rule out (you can turn this off in pause). Listen explains the next logical step when you're stuck, spending one song: you start with 3 and earn another each time you settle a new grove flawlessly. Undo steps back your crosses, and Clear wipes them. Finish with every moon and no hints for a flawless Silent wings mark.

games.title: Gloamglass
games.blurb: Pour luminous night-inks until every phial holds a single hue under the gloaming.
games.description: A mobile-first water-sort puzzle set in a quiet alchemist's loft at dusk. Glass phials hold stacked layers of glowing night-ink. Lift one, pour into another when the top colors match or the glass is empty, and keep going until every phial is either vacant or filled with a single hue. Twenty-four campaign lofts ramp from a two-ink warm-up to crowded ten-color shelves, with hard and super-hard marks mid-campaign. Undo steps back a pour, Shuffle rearranges the phials on the shelf, and Extra phial adds one empty glass once per loft — all free, with no ads or lives gate. Harder lofts add a pour budget; when it runs out you can retry the same layout or spend Extra if you still have it.
games.how: Tap a phial to lift it, tap another to pour. Pour only onto an empty phial or a matching top color with room. Fill every phial with one color to clear the loft. Undo steps back a pour. Shuffle rearranges the phials. Extra phial adds one empty glass once per loft.

games.title: Knotlight
games.blurb: Twist glowing hoops until their gaps slip every clip, and send each freed ring up into the night as a star.
games.description: A mobile-first ring-untangling puzzle under a midnight sky. Neon-glass hoops hang hitched together by small clips. Drag a ring round to turn it, and when its opening reaches a clip the clip slips off. A piece that still owns a clip is pinned, so find the loose end and work inward. Every freed hoop flies up and becomes a star, and a cleared board draws its constellation. Twenty-four boards ramp from a single hitch to twelve-ring knots with brass studs that can't pass a clip, iron pegs, closed rings, sliding bars, and embers that burn down one per move.
games.how: Drag a ring round to turn it; its opening moves with it. A clip is the colour of the piece it belongs to and hooks the other piece. Turn the hooked ring until its gap reaches the clip and the clip slips off. A piece that still owns a clip is pinned and won't budge. A piece with no clips left flies away. Brass studs can't pass a clip or an iron peg, so turn the other way. Closed rings have no gap, so unhook everything around them. Bars slide off along their arrows once they're free. Embers burn down one per move, so free that ring before it hits zero. Hint shows a good move, Snip cuts any one clip once per board, and Undo is unlimited.

games.title: Lullwater
games.blurb: Tap the moonlit keys as they touch the lake, and the night plays its lullaby.
games.description: A mobile-first piano-tile rhythm game on a black mountain lake. Glowing moon-glass keys drift down four lanes toward the waterline. Tap each one as it meets the water and it plays the next note of the song, with ripples, sparks and a lane of light. Hold long keys until their thread of moonlight runs out, tap twin keys together, and never touch the empty lake or let a key sink untouched. Finish a song for a star, and it starts again faster for the second and third stars, then three crowns, then an endless run that keeps speeding up. Seven public-domain songs, from a gentle Little Star to a running Canon of the Small Hours, unlock one by one. The sky changes with every star, from moonrise blue to violet, tide-glass, rose, ember and full aurora.
games.how: Tap a glowing key as it reaches the waterline; each tap plays the next note. Press and hold long keys until the thread of light runs out. Tap both twin keys. Tapping the empty lake, or letting a key sink past the bottom, stops the music. Hitting right on the line scores Perfect (2 points). Clear the song for a star; it restarts faster for 3 stars, then 3 crowns, then endless. One free Second wind per run lets you keep going after a slip. Earn a star on a song to wake the next one.
